title: Sikh Confederacy
capsule: The Sikh Confederacy (the Misls) was a loose alliance of twelve sovereign Sikh chieftaincies that emerged in the Punjab after the decline of Mughal authority and the Afghan invasions of the mid-eighteenth century. Formalised at the Sarbat Khalsa assembly of 29 March 1748, the confederacy repulsed repeated incursions by Ahmad Shah Durrani and came to dominate the Punjab from the Indus to the Sutlej, with Amritsar as its spiritual and political centre. Ranjit Singh of the Sukerchakia Misl systematically absorbed the other chieftaincies after his capture of Lahore in 1799, unifying them into the Sikh Empire and effectively ending the confederacy as a collective entity by 1807.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The collective territorial extent of the Misls is poorly mapped; individual misl domains overlapped and fluctuated, so polygon boundaries represent a scholarly approximation rather than a precise political frontier.
